evaluations.outcome: no_actionable_improvement: evaluated Astro documentation generation across 8 successful docs.yml runs in the 2026-10-02T05:53Z-07:03Z window, plus 3 successful cao-dashboard.yml producer runs (36975515081, 36973400162, 36970747009). Trusted Actions metadata showed zero observable queue time in every sampled docs run, workflow wall-time median 64s with p90 84s, build-job median 42s with p90 55s, schedule-freshness median 7s with p90 7s on 3 scheduled runs, and deploy-job median 15s with p90 17s on the 3 runs that actually deployed. Comparable docs build-step medians were 10s for Build documentation, 5s for Restore node_modules, 2s for Restore cached CAO Dashboard, and 8.5s for Upload Pages artifact; Install dependencies, Save node_modules, Find latest CAO Dashboard run, and Mount latest CAO Dashboard artifact were skipped in all 8 successful docs builds, confirming stable cache hits. Cross-checking trusted producer timings showed Astro-style site generation is also not the bottleneck upstream: successful dashboard build jobs spent 146-161s total, with Upgrade fallback activity data alone taking 102-109s, Install dashboard build dependencies 7-9s, Assess activity database health 11s, Assemble Dashboard Language site just 2-3s, and Upload dashboard artifact 9-10s. Trusted logs from run 36975515081 further confirmed the producer copied a 508.9 MiB gh-aw-logs.sqlite plus 133 activity shards totaling 324.7 MiB into a 48,995,542-byte artifact before upload. Because docs-side Astro generation is only ~10s median and producer-side dashboard/site build is only 2-3s, no Astro-focused change can plausibly save at least 60s or 15% of median docs execution time without overlapping already-recorded reusable-dashboard work.

suggestion-made: duplicate docs workflow_run rebuilds after successful CAO Dashboard completions remain the largest avoidable docs.yml cost in the latest 20-run/8-success sample. Trusted docs metadata showed workflow median 88.5s, build median 45s, deploy median 28s, schedule-freshness median 8s, and two successful workflow_run duplicates on the same SHA consumed 66s and 46s total with deploy skipped. Trusted cache evidence showed setup-node npm, explicit node_modules, and central-agentic-ops-dashboard caches all hit on the measured docs build. Trusted producer timings showed dashboard build remained dominated by Upgrade fallback activity data (119-122s), not by docs-side generation. Recommendation emitted: add a workflow_run freshness gate in docs.yml so same-SHA successful dashboard completions skip redundant docs builds when the latest deployed docs are already current.

no_actionable_improvement: reusable dashboard generation is not the current bottleneck in docs.yml; trusted docs metadata across 7 successful comparable runs shows Restore cached CAO Dashboard median 2s (p90 3.8s) with Find latest CAO Dashboard run and Mount latest CAO Dashboard artifact skipped in every successful docs build, while full workflow median is 86s and build-job median is 51s. Existing open issues #15497 and #15332 already cover the remaining dashboard-input re-upgrade optimization upstream in cao-dashboard.yml, so no new non-duplicate improvement meets the threshold from the current evidence window.

no_actionable_improvement: trusted docs.yml evidence across 9 completed runs (8 successful builds, 1 successful skip-only schedule run) shows packaging and transfer are stable but below the actionable threshold. Queue time stayed 0s median/p90; full workflow median was 66s with p90 91s; build-job median 52.5s with p90 57s; deploy-job median 13.5s with p90 18s; and Upload Pages artifact cost only 11s median with p90 11s. Trusted build logs confirmed three cache hits in every successful build (setup-node npm cache, explicit node_modules cache ~283 MiB, and central-agentic-ops-dashboard cache ~41 MiB), while uploaded github-pages artifacts remained tightly clustered at 55.2-56.1 MiB. Artifact transfer therefore contributes ~21% of build time and ~17% of full-workflow median, far below the required >=60s absolute or >=15% median-execution saving opportunity for a safe workflow-only change. Existing duplication and freshness-gating work remains the materially larger lever; no new non-duplicate packaging recommendation is warranted from this window.
